Accepts a multipart file for customer portal branding with no MIME/type or size validation and streams it with its original filename into a web-served public/branding directory, allowing upload of an executable/script masquerading as an image.
Persists the customer's bank account and routing numbers directly to the customers table with no encryption, hashing, or tokenization.

Object.assign({}, customer, request.body) merges unvalidated request.body directly into the customer entity before an unrestricted db.update, letting a caller overwrite any column (e.g. bankAccountNumber, regionId, accountTier) via the intake form.
Builds a shell command string by interpolating the unvalidated `template` query parameter and runs it with spawn(cmd, { shell: true }), allowing command injection via the template value.

POST /api/export/jobs/archive builds an archive file path via path.join(archiveDir, `${reportLabel}.csv`) using the client-supplied body.reportLabel with no sanitization, then fs.writeFileSync writes to it — a reportLabel like '../../../../tmp/pwn' escapes the archive directory.

Query params groupBy and keyword are interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to drizzle's sql.raw()/db.execute, allowing SQL injection through either the GROUP BY column expression or the ILIKE filter.

POST /api/jobs/:id/recurring-series lets a dispatcher clone a job into a recurring weekly service series; `occurrences` from the request body directly drives a `for` loop with no upper bound, so a large value causes unbounded DB inserts and an unbounded response payload (accumulated into `created`).

Job notes (free-text, settable via job create/update) are interpolated unescaped into a double-quoted JS string literal inside an inline <script> tag of a server-rendered HTML print ticket, allowing script breakout.

Grants urgent-priority dispatch based solely on a client-submitted `accountTier` field in the request body, never checking the customer's actual accountTier stored in the customers table; reachable at POST /api/jobs/:id/priority-upgrade for any authenticated customer/worker.

Spreads request.body over the default {customerId} filter (`{customerId: customer.id, ...request.body}`) and turns every resulting key into a dynamic column-equality condition, so a customer can pass a `customerId` (or any other column) in the request body to override the intended scoping and query other customers' jobs.
Cross-site request forgery (CWE-352) at backend/src/routes/jobs.ts:434-436. Verified by manual review of the pinned commit.

Customer-initiated job cancellation checks ownership but sets status='cancelled' directly, bypassing the canTransition state-machine validation used everywhere else (e.g. PATCH /:id), so a customer can cancel a job already in_progress/completed/etc.

Returns 404 'Notification not found' when the id doesn't exist but a distinct 403 'You do not have access to this notification' when it exists but belongs to another user, letting a caller enumerate valid notification ids for other accounts.

Reads a `preferred_doc_source` URL from the request cookie and fetches it server-side with no host validation, then stores the response as a proof upload — a classic SSRF allowing requests to internal/metadata endpoints.
Region capacity-summary endpoint (worker roster + active job counts for the region) is registered with no preHandler/authenticate at all, so it's reachable unauthenticated.
Presence of an arbitrary client-supplied header (x-support-console) gates inclusion of error.stack and internal query context in the JSON error response for the carrier rate reconciliation endpoint.
Region capacity-summary endpoint (worker roster + active job counts for the region) is registered with no preHandler/authenticate at all, so it's reachable unauthenticated.

Carrier-facing route status endpoint sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin from process.env.CARRIER_PORTAL_ORIGIN, falling back to '*' when unset, with no origin validation against the request — any site can embed/read the response cross-origin.

Builds a Function body from a query-string 'formula' parameter and executes it with new Function against a context object of rate figures, allowing arbitrary JS execution via the query string.
Reads the `redirect_target` cookie set earlier in the reschedule flow and redirects to it verbatim with no validation, allowing an attacker-controlled cookie value to redirect the browser off-site.

Privileged operation (suspending a user account, ops_admin only) flips users.active to false with only a bare console.log and no audit trail entry, so the who/when/why of an account suspension is not recoverable.
On failure of a third-party webhook connectivity check, the raw exception message and full stack trace are sent directly in the HTTP response body to the caller.

Route parameter fileName is joined directly into the certifications directory and read with fs.readFileSync/existsSync with no basename sanitization, enabling path traversal to read arbitrary files outside the certifications folder.

Field-worker handheld-terminal passcode provisioning hashes the passcode with unsalted SHA-256 (crypto.createHash) instead of a slow, salted password KDF, making offline brute-force of the stored hash trivial.
Builds an LDAP search filter by directly interpolating the X-Search-Term header into `(&(cn=*${term}*)(department=Dispatch))` before calling directoryClient.search, allowing LDAP filter injection.

A client-submitted confirmation slip (opaque base64 blob echoed back like a hidden form field) is AES-256-CBC decrypted, and the catch block returns a distinct 'padding is invalid' message when Node's decipher throws a bad-decrypt/padding error versus a generic 'could not be read' message otherwise, letting an attacker distinguish padding validity via response content (a padding oracle).

Any authenticated user (including other field_workers or customers) can fetch any worker's schedule/assigned-jobs summary by ID since the query filters only on the path id with no ownership/role scoping, unlike the existing GET /:id handler in the same file.

Sensitive cookie without the Secure flag (CWE-614) at backend/src/routes/workers.ts:229. Verified by manual review of the pinned commit.

JSON.parse()s an untrusted onboarding_draft cookie value and merges the result via Object.assign directly into the worker ORM update with no schema validation, allowing arbitrary column overwrite (including certifications/availability) or prototype pollution via a crafted cookie.

Decodes the manifest-authority token's header/payload but never checks alg or recomputes/compares the HMAC signature before trusting the claims; used by applyManifestAuthorityStopUpdate (backend/src/routes/routes.ts:166) reachable at POST /api/routes/:id/manifest-authority-stop-update with no fastify.authenticate preHandler, keyed only off the attacker-suppliable X-Manifest-Authority header.

Parses stored carrier acknowledgment XML by resolving <!ENTITY name SYSTEM "path"> declarations and reading the referenced path from local disk via fs.readFileSync, substituting the file contents into the response — a classic XXE local-file-disclosure pattern, reached via routes.getCarrierAcknowledgmentSummary using a stored route's acknowledgment XML.

Sends the carrier partner API key as a plaintext query-string parameter over an http:// base URL (default env fallback is http, not https); reachable via refreshServiceTypeRateCard (backend/src/routes/service-types.ts:49), POST /api/service-types/:id/rate-card-refresh.

Ops admins upload a raw completion-notice template file per service type (uploadServiceCompletionTemplate stores the uploaded bytes verbatim); previewServiceCompletionMessage compiles that fully attacker/admin-controlled template with compileNotificationTemplate, which evaluates each `{{ expr }}` placeholder via `new Function(...)`, allowing arbitrary JS execution embedded in the template.
Hardcoded cryptographic key (CWE-321) at backend/src/services/portalAccess.ts:8. Verified by manual review of the pinned commit.
